hints: Set up the area of $\triangle ADE = \frac{1}{2}(ka)^2\sin(\pi/6) = \frac{1}{4}k^2 a^2$.
Set up the area of sector $ABC = \frac{1}{2}a^2(\pi/6) = \frac{\pi}{12}a^2$.
Equate $\text{Area}(\triangle ADE) = \frac{1}{2}\text{Area}(\text{sector } ABC)$ and solve for $k$.
walkthrough:
Express the area of triangle $\triangle ADE$ with $AD = AE = ka$ and $\angle BAC = \frac{\pi}{6}$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ADE) = \frac{1}{2}(ka)^2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{2}k^2 a^2 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{4}k^2 a^2$$

Express the area of the circular sector $ABC$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } ABC) = \frac{1}{2}a^2 \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{\pi}{12}a^2$$

Equate the triangle area to half the sector area (since $DE$ bisects the area):
$$\frac{1}{4}k^2 a^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{12}a^2\right) = \frac{\pi}{24}a^2$$

Solve for $k$ to four significant figures:
$$k^2 = \frac{4\pi}{24} = \frac{\pi}{6} \implies k = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{6}} \approx 0.7236$$

hints: Set up the general equation: $\frac{1}{2}(ka)^2\sin\theta = \frac{1}{4}a^2\theta \implies k^2 = \frac{\theta}{2\sin\theta}$.
Use the given inequality $\frac{\theta}{\sin\theta} > 1$ to deduce $k^2 > \frac{1}{2}$.
Combine with the constraint $k < 1$ to state the range of $k$.
walkthrough:
Set up the area bisection relation for general angle $\theta$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ADE) = \frac{1}{2}\text{Area}(\text{sector } ABC) \implies \frac{1}{2}(ka)^2\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}a^2\theta\right)$$
$$\frac{1}{2}k^2 a^2 \sin\theta = \frac{1}{4}a^2\theta \implies k^2 = \frac{\theta}{2\sin\theta} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\theta}{\sin\theta}\right)$$

Combine with the given problem condition $k < 1$ to state the full interval:
$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} < k < 1 \quad \left(\text{or } \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} < k < 1\right)$$
